newsitem.title: USA: FDIC survey says US real estate markets improving.
newsitem.headline: FDIC survey says US real estate markets improving.

text.p: Residential and commercial real estate market conditions improved during the three months ended in late July, a Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. survey said Monday.
The survey of 316 bank and thrift examiners and asset managers in the real estate liquidation division of regulatory agencies was conducted in late July, the FDIC said.
The composite index covering residential and commercial real estate markets rose to 68 in July from 67 in April. July's reading was the highest in two years, since 72 in July 1994, the FDIC said.
In the composite index, a reading above 50 indicates more respondents said conditions were improving than declining, while a reading below 50 indicates the opposite.
For local residential markets, 45 percent of respondents reported improved conditions in the latest survey, the same as in April, and up from 28 percent in January, the FDIC said.
On home construction, 44 percent cited above-average levels of home building compared to 38 percent in April.
On existing home sales, 51 percent reported increasing prices compared with 43 percent in April, and 42 percent reported above-average sales versus 33 percent in April.
The existing home sales figures were the highest in more than two years, since April 1994 when 52 percent reported increasing prices and 51 percent reported above-average sales.

More respondents saw improvements in local commercial real estate markets, 38 percent in July compared with 35 percent in April. One percent reported deterioration, compared with three percent in April, the FDIC said.

The survey said assessment of the demand for office space was the most positive since the survey started in April 1991. In July, 28 percent of the respondents saw increased demand for office space, up from 25 percent in April.

Eighty-three percent cited average or above-average sales of commercial real estate, up from 73 percent in April. Forty percent reported increasing commercial sale prices, the most favorable reading to date, compared with 33 percent in April.
In July, 30 percent reported excess commercial supply, down from 35 percent in April. That compared with 86 percent in January 1992, the FDIC said.

"Based on the gains we noted in April and now in July, it seems clear that many real estate markets across the nation improved during the first half of 1996," FDIC Chairman Ricki Helfer said. "The findings of continued progress, especially in the commercial sector, are encouraging," she added.
